Meeting header: 2026-01-22 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jia (SE), Lucas (CSM), Priya (Solutions Eng), Elena (Head of ML - NavaCommerce), Rajiv (Platform), Maya (Security), Tom (Product)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey team, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Elena (NavaCommerce): Elena here.
[00:07] Rajiv: Rajiv.
[00:08] Maya: Maya on security.
[00:09] Tom: Tom here.
[00:11] Jia (Redwood SE): Jia here. Lucas?
[00:13] Lucas (CSM): Lucas present.
[00:15] Samir: Cool. Agenda — short status on onboarding, dig into the KV cache tail latency we saw in last week's benchmark, and finalize the SLO playbook for the staged ramp. Any additions?
[00:25] Elena: Nope, that's it. We're most concerned about the spikes we saw in the P99 when the cache wasn't warm.
[00:30] Jia: Right, and we confirmed on our side the model variant is identical to what we provisioned; the difference was the cache population pattern. I'll walk through the traces.
[00:35] Rajiv: Before that, creds — we still don't have the SCIM SSO piece finalized. The SAML assertion errors from Friday were the blocker for our CI job.
[00:42] Samir: Got it. I pushed a hotfix doc yesterday and Jia has a short troubleshooting checklist. I'll send the updated SAML/SCIM checklist after this call.
[00:49] Maya: Also want to flag KMS policy — we enforce customer-managed keys for any model logs that persist beyond 24 hours. Is that supported for Private yet?
[00:55] Priya (Solutions Eng): We support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we can do envelope encryption and we have an HSM-backed option on our roadmap. We'll capture the specifics in the security pack.
[01:05] Tom: What's the expected gap for host vs private on KMS?
[01:07] Priya: For Private: immediate support. Hosted: we'll need a short letter of intent; timeline likely a couple months for full HSM attestation. We'll note that as a constraint.
[01:15] Jia: Ok jumping to the KV cache issue. We replayed your QA profile and instrumented the runtime. Observed pattern: cold-start tokens cause a KV cache miss cascade, which increases decode time and shows up as P95->P99 tail spikes when traffic has high entropy.
[01:32] Elena: That's consistent with our staging run. We saw average latency ok, but occasional 700-900ms spikes that break our SLOs.
[01:38] Jia: Correct. Two mitigations: 1) pre-warm using a short prefix warmup script that hits the most common prompt families, 2) enable a small edge cache of recent KV entries per worker to reduce cross-worker fetches. We can enable both in staging.
[01:52] Rajiv: How invasive is the edge cache? Does it need a different binary or config?
[01:57] Jia: Config toggle only; default off. We ran it in our internal perf lab — reduced tail by ~45% in similar traffic. But requires slightly more GPU memory headroom. We can quantify for your profile.
[02:10] Elena: Memory headroom is fine as long as latency improves. Our concern is cost — we don't want to jump to a bigger instance family without clear delta.
[02:18] Samir: We'll produce a cost delta estimate. Also note, dynamic batching settings interplay with KV behavior — aggressive batching can exacerbate cold tail if you have sporadic arrival. We can tune batch limits to trade a little throughput for stable latency.
[02:33] Tom: Any risk to model quality from those config changes?
[02:36] Jia: No, purely infra-level. The model outputs are identical; those are runtime optimizations. The only quality impact would be if you change quantization level or switch model variants.
[02:45] Rajiv: About the SLO playbook — we want concrete triggers and playbooks for canary failover. Example: if P99 > 500ms for 5 minutes, shift traffic to a lower-latency model variant or fallback to hosted.
[02:58] Lucas (CSM): We've had customers use exactly that pattern. Our recommended playbook: 1) detect (P99 exceedance), 2) attempt auto-warm (run prewarm), 3) if persists, reduce batch size and pin to lower-latency model, 4) if still failing, failover to hosted for a rolling window while ops triage. We can put this in a runnable runbook.
[03:20] Maya: On the security side, we need audit logs at token level or at least per-request traceability. Does Redwood provide that?
[03:27] Priya: We emit request-level audit logs and can extend retention for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, retention is subject to package. Logs can be integrated into your SIEM via webhook or S3 exports. We'll send the log schema.
[03:37] Maya: Great. Also please include examples of masked-personally-identifiable-information handling.
[03:41] Samir: Noted. We'll include sample redaction rules.
[03:45] Jia: Back to the KV triage, we recommend running the warmup script 15 minutes prior to peak and then a short continuous background prefetch for the first 30 minutes of a ramp. For the POC, we can manage that from Redwood side for the next 2 weeks.
[03:58] Rajiv: Can you do that in staging? We want to see the difference on our workload.
[04:01] Jia: Yes — need staging creds and allowlist IPs; also, please forward any request traces from your run so we can tune the warmup patterns.
[04:10] Elena: We'll share traces; we have obfuscated payloads.
[04:12] Rajiv: Quick note — Friday our CI failed with a TLS handshake error when trying to pull tokens; logs attached to the ticket. Might be IP or SNI mismatch.
[04:20] Samir: We'll triage that after the call. Please share the logs in the ticket and I'll loop in infra.
[04:24] Lucas: Onboarding checklist status quick readout: OAuth tokens created, SSO in progress, SCIM mapping incomplete, staging keys pending allowlist. Looks like two blockers: SCIM mapping and IP allowlist.
[04:39] Maya: I can take the SCIM mapping offline with Samir — we have some custom attributes.
[04:43] Samir: Perfect. We'll set a micro-call if needed.
[04:45] Tom: For the staged ramp schedule, are we still aiming for the week of Feb 2?
[04:49] Priya: That's still realistic if we clear the credentialing and resolve the cache warmup test results this week.
[04:55] Elena: Sounds good. Any updates on pricing or cost guidance if we enable edge cache and bump memory?
[05:01] Samir: We'll share a delta estimate with exact instance-size alternatives. Expect a modest increase — we'll show per-100k token cost models with and without edge cache.
[05:10] Rajiv: One more technical Q — during the last benchmark we saw KV cache thrash across workers causing extra interconnect traffic. Is there a way to pin a conversation to a worker?
[05:20] Jia: We have session affinity in our routing layer as an opt-in feature; that's exactly for sticky workloads. There's a tradeoff for load balance, but it reduces inter-worker syncs. We can enable for your canary to test.
[05:34] Elena: Would that help with our P99?
[05:36] Jia: It should; combined with warmup and edge cache it helps a lot. We observed up to 60% tail reduction in similar conversational traces.
[05:44] Samir: Recap time — action items and next steps: Samir to send updated SAML/SCIM doc and security pack; Jia to share warmup script and enablement notes; Rajiv to confirm allowlist and provide the TLS/callback logs; Maya to confirm KMS policy requirements; team to run 1k-request latency sweep once creds are in place.
[06:03] Tom: Can we also get a short note on rollback playbook if the canary causes regressions?
[06:08] Lucas: We'll attach the rollback steps to the SLO playbook — quick traffic revert and model pin, plus contact matrix.
[06:15] Elena: Thanks everyone — this was useful.
[06:17] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with the docs and proposed time slots for the white-glove session.
[06:22] (end of call)
